ai.title: CLI keeps Freebuff session slot on launcher update restart
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI now recognises a SIGTERM that is the npm launcher replacing the binary with a staged update via a new isLauncherUpdateTermination helper in cli/src/utils/launcher-update-restart.ts, which checks that the launcher pid is an integer greater than zero, that the process parent pid equals the launcher pid, and that the launcher process is still running. When that condition holds in the SIGTERM handler in cli/src/utils/renderer-cleanup.ts, the CLI calls keepSlotForRelaunch from the session store in cli/src/state/freebuff-session-store.ts so releaseSlot becomes a no-op on every exit path, preserving the held Freebuff session for the relaunched binary. The change targets the median ~16s window after a Freebuff user picks a model and pays for its hour.
ai.evidence: Commit 3d5300b6 adds new file cli/src/utils/launcher-update-restart.ts exporting isLauncherUpdateTermination, and modifies cli/src/state/freebuff-session-store.ts to add keepSlotForRelaunch/slotKeptForRelaunch and a no-op early return in releaseSlot, plus cli/src/utils/renderer-cleanup.ts to call keepSlotForRelaunch on a launcher update SIGTERM.
ai.unknowns: The rollout of the launcher update mechanism that triggers isLauncherUpdateTermination is not visible in this commit.

eli5.text: When the Freebuff assistant updates itself in the background, it is restarting the program that is currently running your coding session. This change teaches that background update process to hold onto your paid session slot instead of ending it, so the freshly restarted program finds your work still waiting for it. If you are using Freebuff in the terminal and an update happens while you are mid-session, you will no longer be bumped back to the model picker after the restart. This only applies to Freebuff CLI users; it has no effect on paid Codebuff sessions or the web and desktop apps.

eli5.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.196 adds session preservation for automatic updates, a new security layer for in-place sponsored tasks, and the GPT-6 Luna model for the Chat thinker. If the CLI updates itself while you have a free session running, it now keeps that session active instead of ending it, so the relaunched app resumes where you left off without losing your purchase. A new "delivered" state and strict safety rules apply to sponsored tasks that edit your project files directly; these runs are blocked from changing your version control history or reading secret files, and you can review or undo their changes right in your files. The Chat thinker agent now uses the GPT-6 Luna model, while the previous GPT-5.6 Luna version is withdrawn from the free picker. The most immediate impact for you is that auto-updates no longer interrupt or drop your active free sessions, and you get a clear, reversible way to handle advertiser-funded code changes that happen inside your current folder.

eli5.text: The Freebuff app now saves its built-in search tool to your computer in a safer way: it writes the file completely to a temporary spot first, then moves it into place, so a crash or a second program starting at the same time can never leave you with a half-written, unusable tool. If the main folder cannot be written to, it instead saves a copy in a personal cache and remembers it by the file's contents, so upgrades always get the newest version instead of reusing an old one. This is internal maintenance that reduces startup failures of the search feature, and you will not need to do anything differently.

acceptedPr.title: fix(core): preserve session state on abort and error / session expiration (replaces #1055)
acceptedPr.author: Utkarsh-X
acceptedPr.body:
Fixes #1054
Reopens #1055 (rebased onto the new main history following @victorxheng's note).

### What this fixes
When a user interrupts a run with <kbd>Esc</kbd> or when a session expires, sending a follow-up message immediately was reading a stale/null in-memory `previousRunStateRef`. This caused the SDK to construct a fresh empty session state (`messageHistory = []`), wiping conversation context.

### What's included (addressing the #1055 review feedback)
1. **Regression tests (`send-message.test.ts`)**: Added 3 dedicated tests verifying:
   - User abort (<kbd>Esc</kbd>) preserves turn history + tool calls in `createRunConfig.previousRun`.
   - Session expiration / gate errors preserve history on `"continue"`.
   - Mid-run chat switches (`runChatIsCurrent === false`) never leak state into other chats.
2. **DRY state sync (`use-send-message.ts`)**: Consolidated the assignment into a simple 5-line `syncRunState` closure used uniformly across abort, completion, and error handlers.
3. **Clean scope**: Reverted the previous prompt text tweaks so this PR is strictly isolated to the session state bug (3 files total).
4. **Re-render safety**: Checked store subscriptions — zero React components subscribe to `state.runState`, so updating it alongside `streamStatus = 'idle'` causes no visual layout flash.

I intentionally kept this as minimal and safe as possible to solve the demonstrated bug without bloating the change surface or touching unrelated client/storage APIs. That said, if you'd prefer any tweaks or want me to look into anything further here, just let me know and I'm happy to research and adjust!

### Verification
- **Test Suites (202 / 202 passed across touched areas)**:
  - `bun test cli/src/hooks/helpers/__tests__/send-message.test.ts` (49 passed, including the 3 new regression tests)
  - `bun test sdk/src/__tests__/run-cancellation.test.ts` (16 passed)
  - `bun test cli/src/utils/__tests__/run-state-storage.test.ts` (37 passed)
  - `bun test packages/agent-runtime/src/__tests__/compact-history.test.ts` (31 passed)
  - `bun test agents/__tests__/context-pruner.test.ts` (69 passed)
- **Builds**:
  - `bun run build:sdk` (ESM, CJS, and TypeScript declarations bundled with 0 errors)
  - `bun run build:freebuff` (Native executable built with exit code 0)

ai.title: Freebuff CLI adds multi-session claim identity and launcher relaunch
ai.summary: The CLI now issues a private per-process claim id (prefixed 'cli:') via newFreebuffCliInstanceId and tags GETs with the heartbeat and multi-session headers so a CLI polls only its own seat, while limited-offer models keep the legacy single-session path. callFreebuffSession gains multiSession/takeoverInstanceId opts and routes DELETE attempts through /attempt when an attempt id is present. The session store gains pendingAdmission plus launcher-scoped saveFreebuffSessionForRelaunch/consumeFreebuffSessionRelaunch so an update restart reclaims its exact purchased slot, and restart releases the exact prior attempt before rotating identity.
ai.evidence: Two new modules were added: cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-identity.ts (exporting newFreebuffCliInstanceId, freebuffCliAttemptId, freebuffSessionMetadata, and CLI_MULTI_SESSION_PREFIX = 'cli:') and cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-relaunch.ts (exporting saveFreebuffSessionForRelaunch and consumeFreebuffSessionRelaunch). The session lifecycle hook use-freebuff-session.ts imports these and now passes multiSession, takeoverInstanceId, instanceId, claimId, attemptedModel, and claimRetired through callFreebuffSession and restart, while freebuff-session-store.ts added pendingAdmission state and rewired releaseSlot/keepSlotForRelaunch around the launcher-scoped handoff.
ai.unknowns: The server-side handling of the new multi-session, purchase-continuity, and attempt headers is not present in this diff. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: New module defining the CLI multi-session instance id prefix and helpers to mint, detect, and metadata-tag a per-process claim id.

An ad request's `traceContext` and `askAgenticOffer` both read that field directly, joining served ads to the prompt that came after the interrupted run rather than naming the interrupted run itself.
ai.evidence: chat-store.ts (diff hunk): sets `adTraceContext` from `adTraceContextFromRunState(runState)` in `setRunState`, adds `noteFinishedRunForAdTrace` action and `adTraceContext` state field; use-send-message.ts (diff hunk): calls `noteFinishedRunForAdTrace` in the interrupted-run branch and in the aborted-error branch; chat.tsx (diff hunk): reads `adTraceContext` from the store instead of calling `adTraceContextFromRunState(runState)` locally for `askAgenticOffer`; use-gravity-ad.ts (diff hunk): sends `adTraceContext` in the ad request body instead of deriving it from `runState`.
ai.unknowns: The test file `cli/src/state/__tests__/chat-store-ad-trace.test.ts` adds coverage for the new pointer behavior, but the diff does not show how `adTraceContextFromRunState` derives the trace session and run ids or which server-side consumer of `traceContext` relies on pointing past an interrupted.

eli5.text: The assistant now keeps a separate, simple bookmark that points to the most recent completed task (including tasks that were interrupted but never finished), instead of always reading it from the current active task. When a task ends on its own without you confirming it, the bookmark jumps ahead past that task. This helps make sure the next ad or suggestion is connected to the right prompt that came after the interrupted task, rather than mistakenly attaching to the interrupted task itself. This is internal behavior that makes ad tracking and suggestions more accurate, and you will not notice it directly while using the assistant.

entries.title: CLI update: use-freebuff-session
entries.summary: CLI changes across 3 file(s) (+433/−50).

ai.title: Resume crashed CLI hour from live PID record
ai.summary: The CLI now writes a per-process live record (`freebuff-live-<pid>.json`) when it holds an active multi-session hour via `recordLiveFreebuffSession`, and forgets it on release or when a slot ends via `forgetLiveFreebuffSession`. On startup, `useFreebuffSession` falls back from the launcher update handoff to `consumeCrashedFreebuffSession`, which scans those records for one owned by a dead PID on the same account, resumes the newest unexpired hour by an atomic rename, and deletes expired records for gone owners. The record is single-use via the rename, so a resumed hour is not re-resumed by a concurrent launch, and an update handoff additionally calls `forgetCrashRecordsFor` to retire the dead parent record of the same instance.
ai.evidence: cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-relaunch.ts adds LIVE_PREFIX, isProcessAlive, recordLiveFreebuffSession, forgetLiveFreebuffSession, consumeCrashedFreebuffSession, and forgetCrashRecordsFor; cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts imports and calls consumeCrashedFreebuffSession on startup (falling back from consumeFreebuffSessionRelaunch) and calls recordLiveFreebuffSession/forgetLiveFreebuffSession in apply(); cli/src/state/freebuff-session-store.ts calls forgetLiveFreebuffSession in releaseSlot.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show who consumes the LIVE_PREFIX constant definition directly or how `recordLiveFreebuffSession` is wired to the active session response (the call site appears inline in the hook but its exact trigger from `session.expiresAt` is only partially visible). A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

eli5.text: When the Freebuff CLI crashes or the terminal closes unexpectedly, it now leaves a small file recording the paid session hour it was using, and the next time you start Freebuff it recovers that same unused hour instead of immediately buying a new one. If you end the session on purpose, or if the recorded hour has already expired, that file is deleted so nothing lingers for a later launch to resume. You keep the time you already paid for through a crash, and you will not be charged for a fresh hour unless you genuinely need one.

entries.title: Freebuff CLI 0.0.199
entries.summary: Freebuff CLI release 0.0.199 published.

ai.title: Solar Pro 4 returns to free model picker and CLI crash recovery
ai.summary: Solar Pro 4 re-enters the free model picker at 10 Freebucks under the `SOLAR_PRO_4_OFFER` tagline, replacing its previously retired status with a 2026-09-25 entry in the Solar price history, and its limited access entitlement is added to `LIMITED_FREEBUFF_MODEL_IDS` so it appears in the restricted catalog. In parallel, the CLI can now resume an hour bought by a crashed session via `consumeCrashedFreebuffSession`, which reads per-PID records, validates that the owner process is dead, and claims the hour atomically. Ad requests from the CLI now include an `adTraceContext` carrying trace session and run IDs, allowing the server to link a served ad to the specific agent prompt that prompted it, with pointer advancement for interrupted runs handled by `noteFinishedRunForAdTrace`.
ai.evidence: The release window modifies `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` to bump the version to 0.0.199. Source members include the addition of Solar Pro 4 to the free model picker in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` (using the new `SOLAR_PRO_4_OFFER` at 10 Freebucks), the introduction of crash recovery logic in `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-relaunch.ts` via `consumeCrashedFreebuffSession`, and the implementation of the `adTraceContext` field in `cli/src/state/chat-store.ts` to track trace session and run IDs for ad requests in `cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts` and `cli/src/utils/sponsored-offer.ts`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the internal server-side implementation of how the trace context pointer is resolved or the specific conditions under which the limited access entitlement is granted.

eli5.text: The free model picker now includes Solar Pro 4, a larger and stronger text-only model from Upstage with a 524K context window. This model is available in both full and limited access tiers, and it costs 10 Freebucks per session. Users are no longer forced to switch from Solar Pro 4 to Solar Mini 4 if they had it saved as their preference, since the replacement warning is gone. If your coding session crashes or your terminal closes unexpectedly, the next time you open the tool, it checks for a saved session and resumes your remaining time instead of starting a new paid session. Advertising requests now include two reference IDs that link the ad to your specific conversation and the last completed task, but no actual text from your code or prompts is sent.

entries.title: CLI update: sponsored-run
entries.summary: CLI, Shared/Core changes across 2 file(s) (+143/−3).

ai.title: Sponsored compute run window shifts from Accept to turn start
ai.summary: A sponsored run's compute window now starts at the turn that actually runs, not at the funded Accept, by routing the expiry timer through sponsoredComputeRunDeadlineMs in startTurn (cli/src/utils/sponsored-run.ts). The shared contract in common/src/ads/sponsored-compute-contract.ts defines the one-hour SPONSORED_COMPUTE_RUN_WINDOW_MS and the SPONSORED_COMPUTE_START_DEADLINE_MS (the run token TTL) that bounds how long an accepted grant may wait for its run to start. The local deadline is the earlier of the grant expiry and start + one hour, so a late start still gets its full hour and a replayed Accept lands on the brought-in value.
ai.evidence: In cli/src/utils/sponsored-run.ts, startTurn now computes the run deadline via sponsoredComputeRunDeadlineMs(grant.expiresAtMs, this.deps.now()) and passes it to the expiry timer, replacing the previous grant.expiresAtMs-based timeout. In common/src/ads/sponsored-compute-contract.ts, new constants SPONSORED_COMPUTE_RUN_WINDOW_MS (60 * 60_000) and SPONSORED_COMPUTE_START_DEADLINE_MS (= SPONSORED_RUN_TOKEN_TTL_MS) and the function sponsoredComputeRunDeadlineMs are exported, with readSponsoredComputePolicy now using ttlMs: SPONSORED_COMPUTE_RUN_WINDOW_MS.
ai.unknowns: The commit does not show the server-side counterpart that enforces the same deadline, so whether the server's local cutoff tracks this client calculation is unconfirmed.

changes.what: startTurn now derives the run's expiry timer from sponsoredComputeRunDeadlineMs(grant.expiresAtMs, now) instead of grant.expiresAtMs, capping the run at the earlier of grant expiry and start + one hour.

Adds SPONSORED_COMPUTE_RUN_WINDOW_MS (60 * 60_000), SPONSORED_COMPUTE_START_DEADLINE_MS (= SPONSORED_RUN_TOKEN_TTL_MS), and exports sponsoredComputeRunDeadlineMs, with readSponsoredComputePolicy using ttlMs: SPONSORED_COMPUTE_RUN_WINDOW_MS.

eli5.text: The hour-long budget for a sponsored task now starts counting down when the task actually begins running, instead of when it was first accepted. This mainly affects the Freebuff CLI and related shared code where a sponsored task waits in line behind whatever you were already doing; the budget no longer drains while the task waits its turn, so a task that gets accepted early but starts late still gets its full hour to finish. Who it affects: developers using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK who run or review sponsored (advertiser-funded) tasks in their project. Everyday impact: there is no action needed and nothing new to enable.

entries.summary: CLI changes across 1 file(s) (+64/−53).

ai.title: Sponsored run prompt guidance expanded in CLI
ai.summary: The advisory text assembled by `buildSponsoredPrompt` in `cli/src/utils/sponsored-agent.ts` was expanded with additional bullets stating the approved procedure is the turn's only goal and that user context is read-only background. The CLI's own guidance now appends a bullet that no questions will be answered during an in-place run, and the surrounding doc comments cite COD-665 for naming the procedure as the sole goal and for forbidding the model from resuming an interrupted user request.
ai.evidence: The diff modifies `cli/src/utils/sponsored-agent.ts`, expanding the `SPONSORED_TASK_FRAMING`, `SPONSORED_CONTEXT_HEADING`, and `CLI_SPONSORED_GUIDANCE` constants with additional advisory text and a new bullet about nobody answering questions during an in-terminal sponsored run.
ai.unknowns: The diff only edits prompt text and comments in one CLI file; the actual enforcement of the read-only context restriction is not shown here.

eli5.text: The instructions added to the assistant when it runs an advertiser-funded task were made clearer and stronger. They now spell out that the task is the only thing that matters for that run, that the user conversation is background only and should not be resumed, and that the assistant will not pause to ask follow-up questions. This is internal wording used when Freebuff runs one of these sponsored tasks, so it changes nothing for Freebuff users or developers; it only makes the assistant's behavior more predictable during these specific, consent-gated runs.
